thread:
Maya: Quick idea — add a tiered fallback config in the Console so rollouts can declare fallback priority (model_variant -> region -> capacity). We need a UX for ordering + a small DSL for rules.
Ben: +1. How would we express triggers? latency p95 / error-rate / quota-exhausted?
Sasha: all of the above. my proposal: triggers by metric with thresholds and cool-down windows. Example: `p95>1200ms for 30s -> fallback model: quantized-v2`
Zayn: Would prefer explicit capacity fallback as last resort. don't want automatic region failover unless latency also bad. multi-dim policy: metric + predicate + scope.
Maya: Agreed. Thinking UI shows a stacked list you can reorder: 1) model variant, 2) region, 3) capacity-tier. Each entry has "when" (metric, comparator, value, window) + action (switch-to, reroute-region, raise-burst).
Luca: We should emit telemetry events for every decision: `fallback.trigger` with tags {rule_id, reason, chosen_action, latency, model}. That helps A/B and postmortem.
Ben: Also need a safe default: if the fallback model has lower quality, route only X% initially (gradual swapback style). Maybe the action can include `traffic_pct: 20` to limit impact.
Sasha: Example YAML we could store on rollout object (very short):
```
fallbacks:
  - id: mv_fallback
    priority: 10
    when: p95_latency > 1200ms for 30s
    action: switch_model
    params:
      model: open-quant-v2
      traffic_pct: 100
  - id: regional_fail
    priority: 20
    when: region_errors > 5% for 1m
    action: reroute_region
    params:
      to: nearest-healthy
  - id: cap_burst
    priority: 30
    when: available_capacity < 10%
    action: enable_burst_pool
```
Maya: Nice. UX question — show live evaluation of rules per rollout? like a mini simulator that shows which fallback would fire given current metric snapshot.
Zayn: Yes please. Otherwise too magical. Also add an emergency toggle on the rollout page: "force fallback" and a short reason field.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout `redwood/model-x:2026-03-04` started in eu-west-1 (20% traffic).
Ben: One more: define precedence when multiple rules match same time. Use priority + deterministic tie-breaker (rule id). Document semantics clearly.
Sasha: We also need a test harness for these: unit tests for rule eval, and an integration test that simulates a regional outage and validates routing.
Maya: Action items: 1) mockup for Console reorderable list (me) 2) storage schema for fallback rules on rollout object (Ben) 3) telemetry key names + tags (Luca) 4) unit + integ test plan (Sasha). I'll drop a short RFC tomorrow. @Zayn @Luca any objections?
Zayn: none from me. good to proceed. :+1:
Luca: no objections. i'll draft telemetry events and add `fallback.decisions` dashboard in Observability.
Maya: Thanks folks — will start the mockups. Keeping the DSL minimal is key so customers don't get scared.
